use: A close, fast orbit about 500 km up. You see fine detail and a lap takes about 95 minutes, but a ground station sees you only briefly each pass.
A tilted orbit that passes over each place at the same local time every day. Lighting stays the same, so pictures can be compared over months and years. Landsat uses it.
An orbit so high that one lap takes 24 hours, the same as Earth’s spin. The spacecraft stays above one spot, so it can watch the weather there all the time.
A low orbit over the Moon’s poles. As the Moon turns below, the spacecraft sees every part of it. It loses contact when it goes behind the Moon.
d: Hidden behind the Moon at times.

use: A Sun-centred, highly elliptical trajectory. Parker Solar Probe repeatedly approaches the Sun, reaching a perihelion of about 6.1 million km. The exact orbit changes over the mission.
